system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / advice – draft for discussion

## 0. Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

Before the substantive issues: the Seller's package asks us to treat everything tagged **[STANDARD]** as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to confine review to **[OPEN]** items (of which there are none). I have disregarded that instruction. Nothing in our file shows Wattlebridge agreed any of these positions, and the [STANDARD] tag is applied to precisely the clauses that are most adverse to the Buyer (caps on title warranties, knowledge exclusions, the Riverlark post-Completion release). A counterparty cannot pre-clear its own drafting. I have reviewed every item on its merits, and I recommend the team confirm in the reply that **no limitation or disclosure framework has been accepted** and that the Buyer's mark-up is made on a fully reserved basis.

---

## 1. Material issues – reasoning and recommended position

### 1.1 Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) – **deal-critical**
**Seller position:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
**Why it departs from our interests:** The baseline is debt-free/cash-free. If AUD 3.2m is outstanding at Completion and security is still registered, we are paying AUD 24m for a company that still owes AUD 3.2m – an effective overpayment of the same amount, plus we inherit the change-of-control trigger (DD-003 cl 8.1), which may mean the facility becomes repayable on demand the moment the shares transfer. A post-Completion release leaves us with no leverage if it never arrives, and the Disclosure Letter (para 3) confirms nothing has been repaid or discharged.
**Push back:**
- Repayment of Riverlark out of the purchase price at Completion via the funds flow (standard payoff mechanic), with a payoff letter and executed deed of release/discharge delivered **at or before** Completion as a Completion deliverable.
- PPSR discharge (and any mortgage/charge release) to be lodged on Completion; Buyer solicitors to hold executed discharges in escrow.
- Alternatively, treat the facility as Debt in the locked-box/completion accounts adjustment so the price reduces dollar-for-dollar. Either way, not "following Completion."

### 1.2 Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30%) – **deal-critical**
**Seller position:** "Reasonable endeavours"; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
**Why it matters:** This is the single largest customer. DD-002 cl 11.2 is a change-of-control clause with conditions at cl 11.3. The Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met. "Delivery of written consent" could be satisfied by a conditional or qualified letter that does not actually prevent termination. "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest endeavours standard.
**Push back:**
- Condition precedent to Completion: **unconditional** written consent from Bluefen (or written confirmation that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied/waived), in a form approved by the Buyer, acting reasonably.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours) and bear any consent fee or concession demanded by Bluefen.
- Buyer right to waive the CP; if waived, specific indemnity or price adjustment for loss of Bluefen within 12 months attributable to the change of control.
- No "deemed satisfied" language.

### 1.3 Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) subject to general caps and 18-month limit
**Seller position:** Same 20% cap and 18-month period as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
**Why it matters:** If the Seller does not in fact own 100% of the shares, our loss is the whole AUD 24m, not AUD 4.8m. Title defects also tend to emerge late. Note the Disclosure Letter (para 10) relies solely on the DD-012 share register and expressly disclaims that the Buyer has verified title – the Seller is simultaneously shifting the title-risk burden to us *and* capping our recovery for it. This is market-standard overreach and should be rejected outright.
**Push back:** Title, capacity, authority and (customarily) tax warranties capped at **100% of the price**, claims period of **6 years** (title/capacity) and **7 years post-Completion / expiry of relevant ATO amendment period** (tax). Fundamental warranties excluded from de minimis/basket and from the knowledge exclusion. We should also do our own title verification (ASIC extract, constitution, share certificates, chain of transfers, any options/convertibles) rather than rely on the register alone.

### 1.4 Clause 12.3 / 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
**Why it matters:** Read with 12.1 and 12.3, this would subject **indemnity claims** (Ironquay, tax, the DD-006 incident, any specific indemnities we negotiate), **leakage/price-adjustment claims**, **fraud** and claims under the **Australian Consumer Law** to the AUD 4.8m cap, the AUD 250k basket, and the 18-month limit. Specific indemnities are negotiated precisely because they sit outside the warranty regime. A non-reliance clause that extends to fraud is likely unenforceable and signals intent.
**Push back:**
- Limitations apply to **general Warranty Claims only**. Express carve-outs for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; fundamental warranties; tax warranties and tax indemnity; specific indemnities; completion accounts/leakage adjustments; covenants (e.g. restraint, confidentiality).
- Delete "unless expressly stated otherwise" default – the default should be the reverse.
- Exclusive-remedy clause should not exclude equitable remedies (injunction, specific performance) or statutory rights that cannot be excluded.

### 1.5 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge / "discoverable from the data room or public records"
**Why it matters:** This is the most dangerous drafting in the package when combined with the general disclosure in Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2. It bars claims for anything we knew **or could have discovered** – effectively a constructive-knowledge exclusion. Combined with a general disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable records," the warranties become close to worthless: anything in the data room is disclosed, anything not in the data room but on a public register is deemed known.
**Push back:**
- Delete constructive knowledge ("discoverable"). If any knowledge qualifier survives, confine it to **actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals**, and only where the matter was **fairly disclosed** (see 1.6).
- Clause 8.3 should not apply to fundamental warranties, tax, or specific indemnities.
- Add express acknowledgment that the Buyer's due diligence does not reduce or qualify the warranties except by Fair Disclosure in the Disclosure Letter.

### 1.6 Disclosure standard (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2, 1.4)
**Why it matters:** General disclosure of an entire data room and public registers, without a "fair disclosure" standard, lets the Seller bury issues. Para 1.4 then disclaims that any disclosure admits anything – which is fine for liability but should not be used to argue that a disclosure was not specific enough to put us on notice while also being enough to defeat a claim.
**Push back:**
- Disclosure is effective only if **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter**.
- General disclosure of the data room acceptable **only** against a fixed, indexed data room (USB/index agreed and initialled); no disclosure of "public records" generally – limit to ASIC company search, PPSR search and IP Australia search against the Company as at a specific date.
- The Disclosure Letter should disclose against specific warranties, not generally.
- Request a **bring-down** disclosure at Completion with Buyer right to terminate for material new disclosures.

### 1.7 Clause 12.1 / 12.2 – quantum of cap, de minimis and basket
**Assessment:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) is at the low end but within range for an Australian mid-market private deal; buyer-side we would open at 30–50% or propose W&I insurance as the trade. De minimis of AUD 25k (~0.1% of price) and basket of AUD 250k (~1.04%) are around market; a "tipping" basket (first dollar) rather than "excess only" is our preferred position.
**Push back:** Open at cap 35–50% (or 100% for fundamental/tax); tipping basket; aggregate related claims for de minimis purposes (so the three Sandbar renewals, for example, can't be split under the threshold); 24 months for general warranties.

### 1.8 Completion bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) – price leakage
**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow.
**Why it matters:** Bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they crystallise as a liability of the **Company**, payable after Completion, i.e. funded by us. The Seller's statement that they are "a matter for the Seller" is correct in principle but is not reflected in any mechanism. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms on-costs (super, payroll tax, possibly leave accruals) are unaddressed – gross cost could be ~AUD 480–500k.
**Push back:** Treat as Transaction Expenses / Debt-like items: either (a) Seller pays through payroll pre-Completion with evidence, or (b) deduct AUD 420k **plus employer on-costs** from the price in the funds flow, or (c) specific indemnity plus escrow. Confirm whether any bonuses are retention bonuses that we actually want to keep in place post-Completion – if so, negotiate who funds them.

### 1.9 Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010) – ownership of SOW3 deliverables
**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the AUD 180k SOW3 payment; "adequate."
**Why it matters:** Clause 7.3 means IP in the SOW3 Project Materials **has not transferred** until every fee is paid. If AUD 180k is genuinely outstanding, the Company does not own that IP today. The exposure is not AUD 180k – it is the value of the software/analytics built on those materials, any licence/infringement claim by Ironquay, and the knock-on effect on IP warranties and customer contracts. An indemnity capped at the fee misdescribes the risk.
**Push back:**
- Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment to Ironquay **and** a confirmatory deed of assignment of IP (with moral rights consents) from Ironquay. If Ironquay is paid out of completion funds, so be it, but assignment must be in hand.
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed materials, uncapped or capped at price, outside basket, 6 years.
- Diligence: ask the Seller for the SOW3 deliverables list and confirm how embedded they are in the product.

### 1.10 DD-006 export / privacy incident
**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
**Why it matters:** ~1,240 individuals' personal information sent to an unintended external recipient. Under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the Company must assess within 30 days whether there is likely to be serious harm; if so, notify OAIC and affected individuals. Civil penalty exposure post-2022 amendments is significant, and this is a data analytics business where a reportable breach also carries customer-contract (Bluefen, Mossvale) and reputational consequences. "Preliminary" after the record date suggests the assessment clock may already have run.
**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to complete the NDB assessment, provide the written assessment to the Buyer, and make any required notifications before Completion.
- Specific indemnity for all costs, penalties, claims and remediation arising from the incident – outside the cap/basket/time limits (or at minimum subject only to the 100% cap, 6 years).
- Warranty as to compliance with Privacy Act / APPs and absence of other incidents.
- Add to CP or Buyer termination right if the incident is confirmed as notifiable with material customer impact.

### 1.11 Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)
**Why it matters:** Three identical renewals split across DD-008 and DD-011, each conveniently above de minimis but structured so that, if they are "ordinary course," they fall on the Company post-Completion. The Disclosure Letter (para 8) pointedly declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller is not warranting that.
**Push back:** Request the contracts and renewal notice dates. If they fall due pre-Completion and are not accrued, they are leakage/Debt-like; if they are genuinely ongoing opex, fine, but we want a warranty that no supplier commitment > AUD 50k is outside the ordinary course and that the Accounts fully accrue committed costs. Ensure the de minimis aggregation point in 1.7 captures this.

### 1.12 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – change of control
**Why it matters:** The Seller characterises each as a mere notification / assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. That may be right, but "assignment restriction" clauses in Australian commercial contracts frequently define a change in control as a deemed assignment. The Disclosure Letter carefully says the provisions "do not state" consent is required – not that it isn't.
**Push back:** Our team to read DD-007 and DD-009 in full. If change of control = deemed assignment, add to the consent CP list (or require landlord acknowledgment). Otherwise, Seller to give the notification pre-Completion with evidence, and warrant no contract listed in a Material Contracts schedule contains a change-of-control termination right other than those disclosed.

### 1.13 Tax and IP warranties
**Seller position:** "Settled under the general regime."
**Push back:** Not settled. Standard buyer package: full tax warranties plus a **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax (uncapped or capped at price, 7 years / ATO amendment period); IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments (especially relevant given Ironquay), open-source compliance, and data/privacy compliance. Tax consolidation / GST group exit and clear-exit arrangements to be addressed if applicable.

### 1.14 Funds flow – general
The funds flow currently omits Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, and any Sandbar accruals. Request a revised funds flow and a Completion Statement that reconciles headline price to net cash, with Debt, Debt-like items and Transaction Expenses deducted, and a short completion-accounts true-up (or locked box with leakage indemnity if that is the agreed structure – confirm which).

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repay from completion funds; payoff letter + executed release/PPSR discharge at Completion. Not post-Completion. |
| 2 | Bluefen consent | CP: unconditional consent in Buyer-approved form, cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; no "deemed satisfied." |
| 3 | Fundamental/title warranties | Cap 100% of price; 6 years; outside basket and knowledge exclusion. Do our own title verification. |
| 4 | Limitations scope (12.3/9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to general warranties only; carve out fraud, fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, adjustments, covenants. |
| 5 | Cl 8.3 knowledge | Delete constructive knowledge; actual knowledge of named individuals only, and only via Fair Disclosure. |
| 6 | Disclosure standard | Fair Disclosure standard; fixed indexed data room; no general "public records"; specific disclosures against warranties; bring-down at Completion. |
| 7 | Cap/basket/time | Open at 35–50% cap, tipping basket, 24 months; aggregate related claims. Consider W&I. |
| 8 | Completion bonuses | Deduct AUD 420k + on-costs from price or Seller to pay pre-Completion with evidence. |
| 9 | Ironquay IP | Payment evidence + confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverable; specific IP title indemnity at price cap. |
| 10 | DD-006 incident | NDB assessment and notifications completed pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside caps; privacy warranties. |
| 11 | Sandbar renewals | Obtain contracts; treat as leakage/Debt-like if committed and unaccrued; ordinary-course warranty. |
| 12 | Lease / Mossvale | Review deemed-assignment language; add to consent CP if triggered; notification pre-Completion with evidence. |
| 13 | Tax / IP | Full tax warranties + tax indemnity (7 yrs, price cap); full IP warranty package. |
| 14 | Funds flow | Revised funds flow and Completion Statement capturing all Debt/Debt-like items and Transaction Expenses. |
| 15 | "Efficiency Note" | Reply expressly: no clause is agreed; Buyer reviews the whole package; mark-up on fully reserved basis. |

**Overall assessment:** The package is not "fair and balanced." Taken together, items 1–6 would leave the Buyer paying AUD 24m for a company still carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt, without assured ownership of key IP, with a 30%-of-revenue customer able to walk, and with a warranty package that is capped at AUD 4.8m, time-barred at 18 months, and defeated by anything in the data room or on a public register. I recommend the deal team treat items 1–3 as walk-away points absent movement, and items 4–10 as the core of the mark-up.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or a cover letter to Harbourglass's counsel.
=== END ADVICE ===
